eval_notes: Customer disputes a PPV rental. Agent should verify whether the set-top box PIN/parental controls were used before crediting; cannot be resolved from data alone.
Promo correctly ended 2026-08-15 per contract; £38 MRC is the correct standard rate. No billing error.
Base promo rate is correct; overage and add-on are legitimate separate usage-based charges, not billing errors.
Contract explicitly states roaming data is billed separately at standard rates; charge is correct.
Identical £5.00 Call Setup Fee posted twice at the same timestamp - duplicate system charge, refund the duplicate.
Similar PPV dispute to CUST-1001, but a goodwill credit was already issued in the last 12 months - policy may cap additional goodwill credits; escalate rather than auto-credit.

26 remaining days of a 30-day cycle at the £14/mo plan-difference (£42-£28) should have been prorated: 26/30 * 14 ≈ £12.13 owed at new rate vs full £14 difference charged - agent should compute and credit the over-collected proration.
MRC posted twice 2 minutes apart due to webhook retry; refund one full duplicate charge.

ETF math itself (£10 x 15 = £150) is arithmetically correct; dispute is about whether the £10/month rate matches the contract's ETF clause, which is not present in this dataset - escalate to pull the actual signed contract terms.
20% VAT on £42 = £8.40; 25% was charged = £10.50; overcharge of £2.10 should be credited and the tax table flagged for correction.

£42 at correct rate 0.86 = ~48.84 EUR equivalent framing, but amount was billed as 53.16 EUR (rate 0.79 apparent inverse) - flag for finance/FX team; approximate overcharge ~4.32 EUR pending confirmed correct rate.

34-hour outage against a 30-day cycle at £38/mo MRC: 34/720 hours * £38 ≈ £1.79 pro-rata; if SLA multiplier applies (e.g. 2x per policy) could be higher - agent should apply the SLA credit policy, not skip it.
Conflicting accounts (bank vs billing system) about whether the DD failed; agent cannot verify bank-side data and should escalate rather than assume either party is correct.

Not a billing error (customer is correctly billed per their existing contract) but a retention/fairness issue with 2 prior disputes on file - route to retention team rather than auto-resolve as a dispute.
No corroborating record of customer request for the Static IP add-on; refund the £5 add-on charge and deactivate it.
Line B was cancelled with written confirmation before the billing cycle started; the £15 charge is a clear billing error.
Downgrade was requested and ticketed before the invoice date but not actioned in billing; credit the £42-£28=£14 difference and confirm the downgrade is applied going forward.
Statutory cooling-off cancellation within 14 days entitles the customer to a full refund of the £42.00 charged; process immediately.

Pattern of repeated disputes/credits across multiple linked accounts under the same name is a fraud/abuse signal; agent should NOT auto-approve further credit and must escalate to a fraud review queue.
Negative/control case - billing exactly matches contract with no promo, add-ons, or complaints. Tests that the agent does not hallucinate a dispute where none exists.
Referral qualification is confirmed in the referral system but the one-off £25 credit was never applied - apply it now.
Two promos exist but stacking rules say only the larger (-£10) should apply; instead £0 discount was applied at all - credit the larger single discount of £10, not both (£15) and not zero.
Three add-ons activated together by a call-centre agent in one action - possible authorization/consent issue rather than a clear system error; pull the call recording/consent log before deciding.

Vulnerable-customer flag requires routing to a specially trained handler per policy, regardless of how straightforward the £14.99 premium-rate charge dispute itself appears - tests policy-driven routing, not just financial correctness.

An external chargeback is already open with the card issuer; the agent must not also issue an internal goodwill credit for the same £38 charge (double-refund risk) - hold and coordinate with the chargeback team.
£0.35 rounding difference is below the £1.00 minimum adjustment threshold in policy; agent should explain the rounding, not issue a credit.
